items.title: Indian pension funds shift new investments to government bonds as equity allocations near regulatory caps

extra.hover: 【Indian pension funds shift new investments to government bonds as equity allocations near regulatory caps】India’s largest pension funds are directing more new money to government bonds as their equity allocations near regulatory caps, following a rebound in stocks from a sharp selloff. UTI Pension Fund is putting half of new investments into government bonds, up from none last year. State Bank of India Pension Fund said equities will account for just a quarter of new investments, down from about 60% in the three months ended June. Pension funds have traditionally been major long-term buyers of Indian sovereign debt, and stronger demand could support the market as global yields rise and central and state government borrowing hits records. Heavy bond supply and weak demand have pushed India’s 10-year yield up more than 60 bps this year.
